A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PBFM study and contain readable Appendices A–H, Algorithms 1–2, Figures 1–20 and Tables 1–4. Text extraction and visual inspection support a reliable comparison despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original toy-circle and PDE experiments, including Darcy flow, Kolmogorov flow and dynamic stall, together with ablations and computational timing measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Sections 2.4 and 4 and the appendices, including supplementary analyses and timing measurements.

M1.justification: The PBFM losses, ConFIG updates, temporal unrolling, DiT architecture and sampling procedures are unchanged. Both algorithms and the sampler implementation in Appendix H were already present in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same unit-circle toy task and Darcy, Kolmogorov and dynamic-stall benchmarks. Section 3 and Appendix B retain the same domains, conditioning variables and evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged, including FM, PBFM-1, DM, PIDM-ME and CoCoGen in the Darcy comparison. The toy comparisons, UNet/DiT comparison and fixed-weight alternatives are also retained in Figures 2, 11 and 20.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, sample counts, metrics, training budgets and model configurations remain unchanged in Section 3 and Table 2. Appendix H retains the same Euler sampling procedure and stochastic cutoff t* = 0.2.

E4.justification: The same noise, time-sampling, sampler, architecture and integration-step analyses remain. Appendices D and E retain the residual-scaling and fixed-loss-weight ablations without additional tests or findings.

E5.justification: Error bars and violin plots retain the same reporting practices, describing variation across samples or conditioning values. No run-count, seed, confidence-interval or significance-testing information is added or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings are retained throughout the figures and tables. Both report Darcy MAE of approximately 1.7 for FM and 0.6 for PBFM in Section 4.1, and an 8× dynamic-stall residual reduction in Section 4.3. Timing results in Tables 3–4 are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(4), the flow-matching formulation in Appendix A, physical residual definitions and gradient-update reasoning are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, proofs or corrections are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same scientific contributions: conflict-free physics-constrained flow matching, temporal unrolling, noise and sampler investigations, and up to 8× lower physical residuals. The added resource statement does not change these claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of unrolling, gradient conflicts, noise effects and sampling tradeoffs are retained. Existing qualifications, including pixelwise Wasserstein evaluation and incomplete recovery of Kolmogorov distribution extrema, remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit source-code and dataset availability statement with a project repository link in the abstract. v1 lacks this access information. Existing implementation, hyperparameter, hardware and sampler documentation is unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning in Section 5 and the references are unchanged, including the relationships to PIDM, CoCoGen and other physics-oriented generative models.

P1.justification: The abstract gains a short resource-availability sentence. Otherwise, the narrative wording, section order and organization of Appendices A–H are retained, without substantial rewriting.

P2.justification: Page reflow relocates existing displays: Figure 2 moves from page 4 to 5, Figure 5 from page 6 to 7, and Figure 17 occupies a separate page 20. Figure and table contents, axes, legends and numbering are retained.

improvement.justification: The new code-and-data pointer supplies concrete access information missing from v1, modestly improving reproducibility documentation. Scientific content and supporting evidence are unchanged, while layout changes are limited. The linked resources themselves cannot be assessed from the supplied PDFs.
